name: William Grover-Williams
features: fair skin, dark hair slicked back, dark watchful eyes, narrow angular face, thin lips, slight wiry build, reserved guarded expression
bio: Raced simply as ‘Williams’, an Englishman born and raised in France who won the first Monaco Grand Prix in 1929 in a British racing green Bugatti 35B, beating Caracciola. He took the French Grand Prix in 1928 and 1929 and the Belgian in 1931. In 1942 he parachuted back into France as SOE agent ‘Sebastian’ and ran the Chestnut circuit with Robert Benoist; captured in 1943, he was killed at Sachsenhausen in 1945.
